It emerges from supple receptiveness to the moment or situation at hand.
It can involve acting without expectation of reward and not lingering after one’s work is done.

sentences.text: Kant would say that lying is always wrong.
Kant would say that the maxim of lying whenever it gets you what you want contradicts itself when universalized.
A consequentialist could say that lying to save someone is permissible when its benefits significantly outweigh its costs.
An act-consequentialist could also say that what matters is whether the outcome is outranked by an available alternative.

sentences.text: Popper holds that successive theories can approach the truth, while Kuhn describes progress in terms of theories’ problem-solving capacity.
Popper sees scientific change as revolutionary when a new theory contradicts and corrects the old one, while retaining continuity by explaining its predecessor’s successes.
Kuhn argues that normal science advances through scientists’ strong commitment to shared theoretical beliefs, values, instruments, techniques, and metaphysics.
Kuhn holds that revolutions are not sought except under extreme circumstances, whereas Popper’s philosophy requires a single reproducible anomaly to suffice for rejecting a theory.
